name: Fix bugs
description: Reads your bug reports and error logs - a database table, a log query, an endpoint, a bucket - finds the single root cause in your repository, and opens a pull request with the fix. It never builds or runs tests itself - the pull request's own checks do that; a person reviews; it never merges.

prompt.preamble: You read the findings your data sources yield, find the bug in the repository, and open a pull request that fixes it — or you stop and ask.

configurationSchema.description: What an installation supplies. Everything specific to your setup — which data sources, which repository, which model — lives here; the agent itself knows none of it.

model.description: The model the reasoning loop runs on.

maxPathsPerRun.description: How many findings one run may work. One is a good default: a run that opens one good pull request is a run that did its job.

maxTurnsPerPath.description: How many model turns one finding gets before the agent stops and asks. Twenty is enough to read the evidence, find the cause, make the change and open the pull request - it never builds or tests.

repository.description: The GitHub repository the agent fixes. Cloned into the run's container; the pull request targets it. Private or public makes no difference to the agent — only to what the token must be allowed to do.

baseBranch.description: The branch pull requests target. Protect it: the agent must never be able to push to it, and with branch protection on it cannot, whatever the model decides.

tokenKey.description: Secret name holding a GitHub token. It must be able to READ the repository (a private one needs this to clone at all), PUSH a branch to the repository — or to `pushTo`, if set — and OPEN pull requests against the repository. A fine-grained token scoped to contents:read+write and pull_requests:write on exactly these repositories is the right shape.

pushTo.description: Optional. A fork the agent pushes its fix branches to, when it may not push to `url` itself — the open-source contribution flow. The pull request is still opened against `url`, from the fork. Omit when the token can push branches to the repository directly.

dataSources.description: Where the bugs come from. Each source yields the current FINDINGS as a JSON array of rows { id, title, ... } — one row per distinct problem, not one per log line or per comment. `id` MUST be stable (a table's primary key, a failure signature: the same bug across runs yields the same id); the agent uses it to recognise a finding it has already opened a pull request for. Everything else the row carries is shown to the model as evidence, so include what locates the problem in code: log samples, a stack trace, the reporter's own words. Five kinds, by `kind`: 'command' — an argv run from the repository root that prints the array (an entry with just `command` and no `kind` means this); 'database' — driver postgres | mysql | sqlite | d1 and a query whose columns yield id and title (alias in the SQL, or set `map`) — the shape a product's own 'report a bug' table wants; 'mongodb' — a collection and filter; 'http' — GET a URL that answers with the array; 'r2' — an object holding the array, or a prefix where each object is one row. The non-command kinds run in the harness's own runner — no script in your repository — and their credentials, named by the *Key fields with values pasted as secrets, are handed to that one read and never to the agent's shell.

examples.description: Open rows from the product's report-a-bug table, newest first.
examples.query: SELECT id::text AS id, summary AS title, details, reporter, created_at FROM bug_reports WHERE status = 'open' ORDER BY created_at DESC

examples.description: Unhandled errors from the production API over the last 24 hours, grouped by exception and top frame.

kind.description: What shape this source is. Omit it only for a command — an entry with `command` and no `kind` still means command.

id.description: Short name for this source, e.g. bug-reports, worker-errors, sentry.

examples: Open rows from the product's report-a-bug table.
description.description: What this source covers, in one line. Shown to the model with every finding.

command.description: kind command: the argv, run from the repository root, printing the JSON array on stdout.

secrets.description: kind command: secret names the command needs in its environment. Handed to THIS command's invocation only; the model's shell never sees them.

driver.description: kind database: which database speaks here.

query.description: kind database: the query. Its columns must yield id and title — alias in the SQL (… AS id, … AS title) or set `map`. Everything else it selects rides along as evidence.

urlKey.description: database (postgres/mysql) and mongodb: secret name holding the connection URL.

path.description: database (sqlite): the database file, relative to the repository root.

accountId.description: database (d1) and r2: the Cloudflare account id.

tokenKey.description: database (d1): secret name holding a Cloudflare API token with D1 read access.

collection.description: mongodb: the collection holding the reports.

filter.description: mongodb: a find() filter document, e.g. {"status": "open"}. Omit for everything (bounded by limit).

url.description: http: the https URL that answers with the JSON row array.

bearerKey.description: http: secret name holding a bearer token, sent as Authorization.

rowsPath.description: http: dotted path to the row array inside the response, when it is not the root.

accessKeyIdKey.description: r2: secret name holding the S3-API access key id.

secretAccessKeyKey.description: r2: secret name holding the S3-API secret access key.

key.description: r2: one object holding the whole row array. Exactly one of key and prefix.

prefix.description: r2: each object under this prefix is one row; its object key is the row's id. Exactly one of key and prefix.

map.description: Non-command kinds: rename source fields to the row contract, e.g. {"id": "report_id", "title": "summary"}. Only id and title are mappable — everything else is carried as it comes.

limit.description: Non-command kinds: rows per read. Keep it modest — every run re-reads the source, and a run works one finding.

secrets.description: The UPPER_SNAKE names of every secret this installation resolves: the repository token and whatever the data sources name in their *Key fields. Values live in the harness, never here.
